title: Canonical scalar pullback and bounded-below site mate comparison
statement: For a scheme map f:X→Y and a unital map a:A→B of discrete commutative rings [def-pc-scheme], the scalar/pullback inverse mates on the etale and pro-etale ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] are invertible [lem-sfb-proetale-scalar-pullback-mate-invertible]. Define their forward comparisons to be the inverses. The etale comparison is the normalized representative comparison of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The canonical ambient direct-image mate is that of [def-sf-etale-proetale-ambient-direct-image-comparison]. For qcqs f its component at any bounded-below etale A-complex J is invertible, without finiteness of A. These statements keep the specified mate normalizations.

source.place: Finite rings paragraph, transport of scalar direct-image mates; canonical pullback/scalar and site comparison maps (Stacks 07A4, 0G7E, 09A6).

proof.text: Apply invertibility of the normalized scalar inverse mates and take their inverses; identify the etale result by its representative scalar unit equation and uniqueness.

The qcqs bounded-below direct-image comparison places the target in the comparison image. Comparison adjunction units are invertible at J and at Rf_*J. The triangle equation makes the comparison counit invertible on this image. Iterated mates then show that the specified ambient mate component is invertible.

proof_origin.place: Canonical comparison normalization used in the finite rings paragraph.
